WSP Parsons Brinckerhoff and DNV GL (2015). Industrial Decarbonisation and Energy Efficiency Roadmaps to 2050 - Cement. Report and Appendices, prepared for the Department of Energy and Climate Change (DECC) and the Department for Business, Innovation and Skills (BIS), London, March 2015.

Source = Cement_Report.pdf (main, 94 printed pages) + Cement_Appendices.pdf (appendices A-D, 91 printed pages), one source; moved to this folder as wsp_2015_uk-roadmap-cement.pdf and wsp_2015_uk-roadmap-cement-appendices.pdf. Page numbers are PRINTED page numbers (footer "Page N of M"); "Appendices ... p.N" = printed page in the appendices PDF (Appendix C register pages 84-88). Loaded: the Appendix C options register (12 options) - whole technologies (BAT kiln, oxy-combustion capture, hydrogen fuel, fluidised-bed kiln, alternative cements) in the main file with TRL, capex per representative site and CO2 reduction; remaining options in _measures. Baselines: kiln temperature, UK electricity per t cement. NOT loaded: per-option SEC or fuel use (the report gives none; no GJ/t clinker anywhere), operating costs (excluded by the study), pathway deployment tables and pathway cost totals (Table 8), social/business findings. Traps: (1) capex is per representative site with site capacity NOT printed (12-13 kilns, 10 Mt/yr gives no per-site capacity), so no per-t formula possible; (2) 50% of BAT replacement cost attributed to decarbonisation in the pathway model; (3) carbon-capture capex (GBP 100m) is capture alone, oxy-combustion; electricity use +100%; (4) the sign of the electricity-reduction column is positive = saving, negative = more electricity; (5) UK production is 8.6 Mt on p.2 but 11.6 Mt on p.23; (6) all costs are order-of-magnitude (Sect. 4.7.3). The report states the price base as 2015 present-day value (Sect. 4.7.2), so 2015_GBP is used. Heating-value basis never stated.
